title: Mint Pear Drop Earrings
category: Earrings (rigid stud-drop climber: a 4-stone pear cluster on a straight post with butterfly back, sold as 1 pair; 8 stones in all, 6 clear and 2 mint)
metal: 18k gold tone (listing: PVD 18K gold coating, anti-tarnish, on surgical stainless steel), bright polish, fine ball-tipped claws; one tone only. Photo 02 tints it rosy; ignore that.
lock: 1 pair of studs. Each: 3 small clear pear-cut cubic zirconia, points up, step down a diagonal sweep from a post with butterfly back, each in 3 ball-tipped claws; beside the lowest, 1 larger pale mint-green pear (7 mm wide), point up, in claws over an open gallery. 18k gold tone, polished. The mint pear must stay beside the lowest clear pear, never hanging centred below a straight 4-stone line.
morph: The arrangement. The listing text ('a short curved line of three small clear pear-cut stones leads down to one larger pear') reads like a straight vertical 4-stone drop, so image models hang the mint pear centred under a line of 3 clear stones, or stretch it into a chandelier on jump rings. On the real piece (05 supplier photo, matched by 01 and 03) the 3 clear pears step down a gentle diagonal and the mint pear sits beside the lowest one, its point tucked in at the joint between the 2nd and 3rd clear stones, finishing a little lower. It is one rigid soldered cluster: no links, no swing (in video it must not sway like a dangle). Photo 02 already drifted: the mint sits on the other side of the column and the piece is about 2x too big. Second risk: scale. Earlier plates drew it 1.6x (colour50 42a/42b) and about 3x (Edition Two 'nimbu pani' ad, rejected for it). Third: colour. Models push 'mint' to blue mint or aqua, or push the green to emerald, saturated lime or olive (02 leans olive). The true stone is pale, bright, transparent green leaning slightly yellow (01, 03), fresher in 05. Fourth: they add a halo, bezel or pave, turn the clear pears into rounds or marquises, flip the pears point down, or draw only 2 clear stones (03 hides the 3rd behind the mint).
sizeMm: About 18 mm long, top claw to the bottom of the cluster (listing and size guide, 'give or take 1 mm'); listed weight about 2.7 g. Mint pear 'approximately 7 mm' (listing); the size guide's 7 mm bar measures its width. Against the guide's 18 mm bar (about 17.8 px per mm on the saved 1400 px refs/.../05.jpg), the mint pear is about 7 mm wide and 10 mm long and each clear pear about 3 x 5.5 mm. The old Edition Two kit and ad facts said 22 mm with a 9 mm mint; that is superseded. Body referent: worn, the top clear pear sits on the lobe over the piercing and the mint pear ends just below the lobe (listing: 'falls just below the lobe'). The whole earring is a little shorter than a Rs 1 coin is wide (20 mm), and the mint pear is about the size of a green pea, a little smaller than a green cardamom pod. Photo 02 draws the earring at about 0.6 of the ear's height (true is about 0.3), so it is about 2x too big: never take scale from it.
mediaIdSource: Fresh Higgsfield imports on 2026-11-20 from the listing's Shopify CDN images (01.jpg = cd17d6d9 packshot, 03.jpg = bf4a0203 macro). ads-500 products.md has no section for this handle, concept-50 plan.json has no lock for it, and there are no ads-500 or concept-camps refs for it. 01 and 03 were made in the Edition Two kit from the supplier photo (YF7034); they match its construction. The kit's 'worn, close detail' image (044461d7) is no longer on the listing.
claims: Waterproof, Tarnish Free, Hypoallergenic (all 3 are tags; the care text also says 'Waterproof and tarnish free, so daily wear and water are fine', and the details list 'PVD 18K gold coating, anti-tarnish' on surgical stainless steel). Not tagged pre-order.
variants: 1 variant: Default Title, 18k gold tone, stock 17. No rhodium silver tone option; every photo shows gold tone (02 reads rosy). Photos (concept-50/refs/mint-pear-drop-earrings/): 01 packshot, the pair three-quarter on a cream plaster block. This is the construction authority and ref 1: 3 clear pears stepping down per earring (the 3rd partly under the mint), the mint pear at the end of each sweep, posts and butterfly backs, true 18k gold tone. 02 worn profile, hair tucked back, mustard satin slip: DRIFTED (about 2x too big, rosy metal, mint on the wrong side of the column). Use it for pose and mood only, never as a reference. 03 macro of one earring on the plaster edge: the sharpest ball claws, open gallery, post and butterfly back, and the true pale green. Ref 2 (detail; the butterfly back gives scale). From this angle only 2 clear pears show, so don't count from it. 04 blush Naira Petite gift box with ribbon, no earrings. 05 size guide: the supplier's own white-ground photo with 18 mm and 7 mm bars and title text. It is the truth for arrangement and size; use it to measure only, because its text and bars would leak. In 05 the two earrings are mirror images (mints facing each other); in 01 both mints sit to the right. Show the pair as in 01, or mirrored as in 05, as long as each mint ends its own sweep.
story: 'Three small lights, then one of mint' (the listing's own line). It reads as a tiny sprig: three clear leaves stepping down to one pale green fruit, literally a pear on a branch, at a size that sits right at the lobe. It is the one soft colour in an otherwise bright gold-and-ice piece, so it reads fresh rather than loud. It rhymes with a green nashpati (colour50 plate 42, 'Pick of the pears', scored 9.0 once the scale was fixed with a pear seed beside it), fresh peas in a split pod (a row of small rounds, then one), pista and pistachio-green sweets, green cardamom, matcha, sea glass, and pastel mint mehendi-season outfits (it is wedding season). The listing's styling tip is hair tucked back with a white or ivory neckline so the mint reads; mint against the blush gift box (photo 04) is a ready palette. The Edition Two 'Cooler than nimbu pani' idea was liked but failed on scale, so any prop must be small (a seed, a pea, a cardamom pod) or the earrings cropped tight.
copyNotes: Use: 'Mint Pear Drop Earrings', 'pale mint green', 'pear-cut', 'three clear pears', 'one of mint', 'cubic zirconia', 'fine claws', '18k gold tone', 'PVD 18K gold coating', 'surgical stainless steel', 'about 18 mm', 'falls just below the lobe', 'post with butterfly back', 'waterproof', 'tarnish free', 'hypoallergenic', 'Edition Two', 'Rs 1,049' / '₹1,049' (the live price; launch copy used ₹1,499 and the colour50 set ₹1,199). Avoid: 'peridot', 'emerald', 'green tourmaline', 'aquamarine', 'jade', 'gemstone', 'diamond' (it is cubic zirconia; those words imply a stone claim and pull the wrong green), 'emerald-green cubic zirconia', 'aqua' or 'teal' (the stone is not blue), bare 'gold', 'solid gold' or 'real gold' (say '18k gold tone'), 'huggie', 'hoop', 'chandelier', 'dangle' or 'swinging' (it is a rigid stud-drop), 'pave', 'halo' or 'bezel' (it is claw-set), '22 mm' or '9 mm stone' (old figures). Do not say pre-order. Water imagery is allowed (it is tagged waterproof), but keep any prop small enough that the 18 mm earring still reads true to size.

scaleRef.use: Add as reference 3: "Reference 3 shows this exact pair beside the listing's own 18 mm and 7 mm size-guide bars at true size (each earring about 18 mm long, the mint pear about 7 mm wide and 10 mm long: a little shorter than a Rs 1 coin is wide, the mint pear about the size of a green pea; worn, the top clear pear sits on the lobe over the piercing and the mint pear ends just below the lobe, about a third of the ear's height): match that scale exactly; copy only the scale, never the bars, their labels or a face."
